blocks.heading: Biggest Earners in Devops Actually Scale

items.text: A DevOps job can plateau exactly like any other job, a generalist pipeline-maintenance role at an IT-services firm has a real, fairly low ceiling.

Platform engineering, building the internal tooling that lets other developers self-serve deployments, is currently the fastest-growing DevOps-adjacent specialisation in Indian product and GCC hiring, and it pays a real premium over generalist pipeline maintenance.

An engineer who can cut a company's cloud bill by 20% with documented reasoning, or who owns a service's SLO and error budget end to end, is worth more than someone holding AWS, Azure, and three vendor badges with no real production ownership behind any of them.

items.text: The honest comparison is not "which credential sounds best." It is which route gets you to one real, provable piece of infrastructure work fastest, for the least unnecessary spend.

visuals.heading: Real Pay, Fresher to Lead

rows: Fresher, IT services company, 0-1 year
Rs 3.5-5.5 LPA
The realistic floor for a fresher with no home-lab proof, mostly service-desk-adjacent and support-heavy DevOps-in-name roles at large IT-services firms.
Fresher, mid-tier product company, 0-1 year
Rs 6-10 LPA
Needs a real portfolio, a hand-built CI/CD pipeline, Terraform-provisioned infrastructure, a working Kubernetes deployment, not certificates alone.
Fresher, unicorn or strong GCC bench, 0-1 year
Rs 9-18 LPA
The exception, not the median. Reserved for candidates who combine a real project with a company that runs serious cloud-native infrastructure in-house.
Early career, IT services, 2-3 years
Rs 6-14 LPA
Progresses slower than product-side pay because most IT-services DevOps work stays close to ticket-driven operations rather than infrastructure ownership.
Early career, product company or GCC, 2-3 years
Rs 14-35 LPA
The gap between IT services and product/GCC pay widens sharply here, this is usually where a deliberate service-to-product move pays off the most.
Mid-level, 5 years, IT services
Rs 14-22 LPA
A real ceiling exists in most services-company DevOps tracks around this stage unless the role shifts toward architecture or client-facing delivery ownership.
You are choosing DevOps mainly because it sounds like "cloud" and pays well, without checking the operational reality

Real DevOps work is pipeline debugging, infrastructure-as-code review, and incident response, not a vague "cloud" job title. The pay is genuinely strong, but it is attached to real operational weight.
You want predictable 9-to-6 hours with zero after-hours responsibility

Most DevOps and SRE roles carry some on-call rotation. Teams with mature processes spread this fairly, but a role with genuinely zero after-hours responsibility is the exception, not the norm, in this field.
You prefer deep, narrow specialisation over a wide, connected tool surface

This field spans Linux, networking, one or two clouds, containers, orchestration, infrastructure as code, and observability by design. If narrow, single-tool depth is what genuinely energises you, a specialist engineering or data role may fit better than the DevOps generalist core.
You are hoping a certification alone gets you past the entry-level filter
A resume with cloud badges and zero GitHub repositories or home-lab proof reads as exam-taking, not demonstrated skill, to most product-company and GCC interviewers.

items.text: Routine log analysis and first-pass alert correlation, AI-assisted observability tools now triage a large share of the noisy, low-value alerts that used to eat a DevOps engineer's morning.
Boilerplate script and pipeline-config generation, tools like GitHub Copilot speed up writing a Terraform module or a CI/CD YAML file from a known pattern.
First-draft infrastructure documentation and incident-summary write-ups, the repetitive documentation work that historically got skipped under deadline pressure.
